claim: Argo Workflows persists workflow execution state directly in Kubernetes Workflow CRDs, updating NodeStatus trees during level-triggered reconciliation loops with optimistic ResourceVersion concurrency control.
mechanism: WorkflowController watches Workflow and Pod resource events via informers. Each reconciliation pass (wfOperationCtx.operate()) evaluates template dependencies, advances node states in Workflow.Status.Nodes, and commits updates via Kubernetes API. On 409 Conflict, the workflow is requeued for a fresh pass.
applicabilityConditions: All Argo Workflows executions on Kubernetes
localContext: WorkflowController watches Workflow and Pod resource events via informers. Each reconciliation pass (wfOperationCtx.operate()) evaluates template dependencies, advances node states in Workflow.Status.Nodes, and commits updates via Kubernetes API. On 409 Conflict, the workflow is requeued for a fresh pass. Known limits: Workflow CRD size is bounded by Kubernetes etcd 1.5MB object size limit; large workflows must enable status offloading to SQL database.

claim: Pod execution decouples main containers from orchestration concerns by injecting argoexec init and wait containers that handle artifact pulling, process lifecycle monitoring, exit code harvesting, and artifact offloading.
mechanism: createWorkflowPod injects argoexec init container (downloads input artifacts from S3/GCS to emptyDir) and argoexec wait container (monitors main container PID, captures exit code, uploads output artifacts, and sets pod annotations for the controller).
applicabilityConditions: All container and script templates executed as Kubernetes Pods

claim: Cross-workflow and step-level concurrency limits are coordinated via ConfigMap-backed semaphores and mutexes where slots are acquired and released atomically.
mechanism: syncManager interacts with Kubernetes ConfigMaps recording active holder keys. internalSemaphore.Acquire appends holder keys if current count < limit; Release removes holder keys unconditionally, ensuring slots are not leaked even if limit fetching fails.
applicabilityConditions: Templates with synchronization.semaphore or synchronization.mutex configurations

claim: Controller high availability uses Kubernetes Leader Election leases to guarantee that exactly one active controller instance reconciles workflow workqueues.
mechanism: Controller instances contend for a Kubernetes Coordination Lease (or ConfigMap). Only the winning leader starts informer event workers and processes the workflow workqueue; standby instances wait in lease renewal loops.
localContext: Controller instances contend for a Kubernetes Coordination Lease (or ConfigMap). Only the winning leader starts informer event workers and processes the workflow workqueue; standby instances wait in lease renewal loops. Known limits: Failover latency depends on lease renewal duration (default 15s) upon unexpected leader node crash.
